metadata.description: EigenLayer is a restaking protocol on Ethereum. Users deposit liquid staking tokens such as stETH, ETHx and mETH into strategy contracts, or point their validators' withdrawal credentials at EigenPods, and that stake then secures Actively Validated Services (AVSs). The core contracts sit behind upgradeable proxies. Core upgrades go through a 10-day timelock, and bEIGEN upgrades go through a separate 24-day timelock. The EIGEN token itself is upgraded on the 10-day path. A 1-of-7 Pauser Multisig can pause every strategy without any delay, freezing $889.90M in restaked LSTs and EIGEN, and it can also pause native ETH restaking through EigenPodManager. Only the Executor Multisig can unpause. It is a 1-of-2 Safe whose two signers are the 10-day Timelock and the 9-of-13 Community Multisig. Every supported LST is a direct dependency, so a failure or compromise of one of those token contracts affects the strategy that holds it.

admins.name: EigenLayer Pauser Multisig (1-of-7)
admins.description: Can call pause() and pauseAll() on all 13 strategies (the 12 StrategyBaseTVLLimits pools and the EIGEN Strategy), on DelegationManager, StrategyManager, AllocationManager, RewardsCoordinator, AVSDirectory, and on the other contracts that use the EigenLayer PauserRegistry. A pause blocks deposits and withdrawals on the affected contracts until the Executor Multisig, the only unpauser, lifts it. The Operations Multisig and the Executor Multisig are registered pausers as well. Capital that can be frozen this way: $889.90M.

admins.name: EigenLayer Operations Multisig (3-of-6)
admins.description: Holds PROPOSER_ROLE and CANCELLER_ROLE on both timelocks (the 10-day core timelock and the 24-day bEIGEN timelock), and is a pauser in both the EigenLayer and EigenDA PauserRegistries. It owns RewardsCoordinator, EmissionsController, StrategyFactory, CrossChainRegistry, OperatorTableUpdater and TaskMailbox, and it is the proofTimestampSetter on EigenPodManager. That lets it change the rewards updater, fee recipient and activation delay, add or remove deposit-whitelisted strategies through StrategyFactory, and set the Pectra fork timestamp that EigenPods use to validate proofs for all native restakers ($6.12B). Its detected reach of $889.90M comes from the strategies it can pause. It has no direct upgrade rights. Upgrades it proposes wait 10 days in the timelock, and the Protocol Council executes them.

mitigations.description: Sets the delay between submitting a root and claims opening on it. Each root stores its activation time when it is submitted, so a change only affects later roots. mitigations.label: future-fee-redirect

mitigations.label: role-grant

admins.name: EigenLayer Executor Multisig (1-of-2)
admins.description: The only unpauser for EigenLayer, and the direct owner of StrategyManager, EigenPodManager, AVSDirectory, the EIGEN and bEIGEN tokens, and all three UpgradeableBeacons (EigenPod, StrategyBase and DurationVaultStrategy). It also owns the main EigenLayer ProxyAdmin (0x8b9566), which upgrades all 31 core proxies, including DelegationManager, StrategyManager, AllocationManager, EigenPodManager, EmissionsController, RewardsCoordinator and the 12 StrategyBaseTVLLimits pools. Through the EigenPod beacon (0x5a2a4F) it could install an implementation that forges or blocks withdrawal proofs for every native restaker, which puts the full $6.12B of natively restaked ETH in scope. The detected reach of $889.90M only counts the LST and EIGEN strategies, because native ETH is tracked through an aggregate figure and the engine does not attribute it automatically. The 1-of-2 threshold looks weak, but neither signer is a person. EigenLayer's docs call this Safe the Executor Multisig, and its two signers are the 10-day TimelockController (0xC06Fd4) and the 9-of-13 Community Multisig (0xFEA470). So every action needs either a timelocked proposal, queued by the Operations Multisig or the Protocol Council and executed by the Protocol Council after 10 days, or an emergency action signed by 9 of the 13 Community Multisig members, which skips the timelock.

admins.name: StrategyFactory
admins.description: Deploys new strategies as beacon proxies and is the strategyWhitelister on StrategyManager. As an admin, its only power is adding strategies to the StrategyManager deposit whitelist or removing them, on behalf of its owner, the Operations Multisig. Removing a strategy stops new deposits, while existing balances and withdrawals keep working.

admins.name: RewardsCoordinator Updater (EOA)
admins.description: The EOA set as rewardsUpdater on the RewardsCoordinator. It submits distribution roots with submitRoot and can disable a root with disableRoot before it activates. A new root becomes claimable 7 days after submission, and during that window the updater can still disable it. It has no direct access to restaked LSTs.

mitigations.label: activation-delay-bound
mitigations.description: A submitted root becomes claimable after the activation delay, currently 7 days. Until then the rewards updater can disable a bad root with disableRoot. After activation, claims against the root can no longer be stopped this way.

mitigations.label: root-veto
mitigations.description: Disables a distribution root before it activates, so nobody can claim against it. Only the rewards updater can call it, and only while root submission is unpaused. It moves no funds.

admins.name: EIGEN Incentive Council (3-of-5 Multisig)
admins.description: The incentiveCouncil of the EmissionsController. It adds and updates the distributions that decide where the weekly EIGEN emissions go across AVSs and strategies. It also receives any EIGEN left in the EmissionsController when sweep() is called. Anyone can call sweep(), and the tokens always go to the council. The RewardsCoordinator sends its protocol fee share to this Safe as well.

mitigations.label: future-emissions-only
mitigations.description: Adds a distribution that starts in a future epoch. The council can send future EIGEN emissions to recipients it chooses, up to the configured per-epoch emission rate. Balances that already exist stay out of its reach.

mitigations.label: future-emissions-only
mitigations.description: Changes an existing distribution for future epochs, leaving past emissions as they were. The risk matches addDistribution.

admins.name: EigenDA EjectionManager
admins.description: EigenDA contract that removes operators from quorums by calling ejectOperator() on the RegistryCoordinator, within configured rate limits. The EigenDA Operations Multisig owns it. Ejection changes who participates in EigenDA quorums and leaves restaked balances and withdrawal rights untouched.

admins.name: EigenDA Operations Multisig (2-of-4)
admins.description: Owns EigenDAServiceManager, the RegistryCoordinator and the other EigenDA contracts. It sets quorum parameters, the churn approver, the ejector, the staleStakesForbidden flag, batch confirmers and the rewards initiator. It also owns the EigenDA ProxyAdmin (0x8247EF), which upgrades the 11 EigenDA proxies, and PaymentVault, whose balance ($6.23K) it can withdraw to itself. It has no access to restaked LST balances.

mitigations.label: role-management
mitigations.description: Sets the address that approves operator churn, which is when a new operator replaces an existing one in a full quorum. A malicious approver could let bad operators push out honest ones. That affects EigenDA correctness, and no restaked funds move.

mitigations.label: role-management
mitigations.description: Sets the ejector on the RegistryCoordinator, currently the EjectionManager. Like EjectionManager.setEjector, it manages EigenDA membership and moves no funds.

mitigations.label: role-management
mitigations.description: Sets the address that creates reward submissions for EigenDA. Submissions are paid from the initiator's own balance, so this role cannot take funds from the protocol.

mitigations.label: rewards-redirect
mitigations.description: Calls RewardsCoordinator.setClaimerFor for EigenDA as an AVS. The new claimer can collect the AVS's accrued rewards through processClaim until the owner changes it back. Owner is the EigenDA Operations Multisig (2-of-4).

mitigations.label: role-management
mitigations.description: Adds or removes an address allowed to call confirmBatch. A malicious confirmer could confirm incorrect data-availability batches. That harms EigenDA correctness, and no restaked funds move through it.

mitigations.label: future-only-validity-check
mitigations.description: Turns the rule that rejects batch signatures based on stale stake on or off. It changes data-availability checks only, and no funds move.

mitigations.label: proxy-admin-upgrade
mitigations.description: Upgrade authority for the 11 EigenDA proxies, including BLSApkRegistry, the disperser, relay and threshold registries, and EigenDAServiceManager. A malicious implementation could break operator registration, ejection or batch confirmation. Owner is the EigenDA Operations Multisig (2-of-4).

Its two signers are the 24-day bEIGEN TimelockController (0x738130) and the 9-of-13 Community Multisig (0xFEA470), so a bEIGEN upgrade waits 24 days unless the Community Multisig acts in an emergency. dependencies.description: Frax's staked frxETH, held in the sfrxETH strategy and worth $8.60M. sfrxETH is an ERC-4626 vault over frxETH with no upgrade mechanism, so the main risk comes from frxETH and Frax governance upstream. The strategy uses the ERC-20 interface.

dependencies.description: The stETH strategy holds users' Lido staked ether, $617.53M of restaked LSTs. EigenLayer calls balanceOf() and transfer() on stETH for deposits and withdrawals, so a stETH upgrade or freeze would hit every user with stETH restaked on EigenLayer.

dependencies.name: ETHx (Stader)
dependencies.description: The ETHx strategy holds Stader's liquid staking token, $141.88M of restaked assets. EigenLayer calls balanceOf() and transfer() on ETHx. A problem in the ETHx contract, or a governance action on it by Stader, would affect restakers in this strategy.

dependencies.name: OETH (Origin Protocol)

governance.proposalRequirements: Proposals start as ELIPs on forum.eigenlayer.xyz. On-chain, only the Operations Multisig (3-of-6 Safe) and the Protocol Council (3-of-5 Safe) hold PROPOSER_ROLE on the core timelock. The Protocol Council is the only EXECUTOR_ROLE holder and the Operations Multisig holds CANCELLER_ROLE. The Community Multisig (9-of-13) holds TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE and signs for the 1-of-2 Executor Multisig that owns the ProxyAdmin, so it can skip the timelock in an emergency.
governance.votingProcess: An ELIP is discussed on the forum. The Operations Multisig or the Protocol Council then queues it in the core timelock, where it waits 10 days before the Protocol Council (3-of-5) executes it. The Operations Multisig can cancel a queued action, and the Community Multisig (9-of-13) can act without delay in an emergency.
